clue.text: Not many voters out in storm: it could ruin the night

parts.note: a low turnout at an election is a light poll

indicators.note: to storm is to rage wildly, so the two little words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Few voters turn out on a stormy night, and the weather threatens to spoil the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' turns OUT IN into UTION, added after LIGHT POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare from street lamps and buildings washes out the stars, spoiling the darkness of the sky after sunset.

clue.text: Repossessed house and office

parts.note: a home taken back by the lender is real estate its owner has forfeited; and the same two words, followed by 'office', name the counter where mislaid belongings are kept

explanation.surface: A bank takes back a home and a business premises.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a pair of seized buildings; the answer plus 'office' is the station desk where found umbrellas wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is real estate, and a house seized by creditors is real estate its owner has forfeited; the phrase also names mislaid belongings handed in.

clue.text: Working month taken up with fertiliser

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking the pieces up means writing them from bottom to top

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on
Aug is the short form of August

explanation.surface: A gardener spends a busy month spreading manure on the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' writes ONAUG backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Seabird droppings piled on coastal islands have long been dug and sold as a rich nitrogen manure.

clue.text: That elementary particle finally revealing signature in air

parts.note: 'that' and 'the' both point to a particular thing, as in 'that man' and 'the man'
a meson is a subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word revealing

explanation.surface: A physicist's discovery of a particle sounds like a grand reveal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signature' is a musical one: the tune that identifies a programme on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature tune is the recognisable melody that introduces a broadcast show, its identifying music on the airwaves.

clue.text: Produce more veg than what pokes out of the ground

definitions.meaning: to ... a rival grower is to harvest a bigger yield

definitions.text: what pokes out of the ground
definitions.meaning: rock exposed at the surface, standing above the soil

explanation.surface: A competitive gardener outgrows a neighbour while shoots break through the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists call bedrock showing at the surface by this name; read as a verb it means beating someone's harvest.

clue.text: Shoot dead, holding automatic at first in both hands

parts.note: the late king is the dead king

indicators.note: in places the single letter between the two hand letters

parts.note: R and L, right and left

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of automatic

explanation.surface: A gunman fires, an automatic weapon in each hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' is botanical, not ballistic; 'holding' only joins LATE to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call a side branch growing from the main stem a lateral, a shoot off the leader.

clue.text: Worked in bathroom perhaps — it's over light

indicators.note: over signals turning the word round

parts.note: the word it, with the 's (is) as a link
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small lamp

explanation.surface: A decorator's bathroom job is done and the light goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the definition but is the lamp; in a down light 'over' means the reversed IT sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathrooms are commonly finished with ceramic squares fixed to walls, so a fitter has worked there in this way.

clue.text: One attending Macbeth in poorer age made to suffer

indicators.note: the words are tormented into a new shape, a rearrangement signal

explanation.surface: A theatregoer at Macbeth during hard times endures a painful evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi wrote an opera of Macbeth, so a member of its audience fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the audience at Verdi's Macbeth is a patron of the lyric stage.

clue.text: Satisfy a companion to S. Beauty?

definitions.meaning: Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty is partnered by his other ballet Swan Lake, abbreviated in the same style to S. plus the second word

explanation.surface: A beauty's companion asks to be satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Quenching a thirst or desire means fulfilling it, which is satisfying it.

clue.text: Everything carried round is smashed

indicators.note: the carrying word goes round the other

parts.note: to tote is to carry
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything someone was carrying has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A car wrecked beyond repair is written off, a sense chiefly American and colloquial.

clue.text: Hurried up a stay in bed, worried for the NHS etc

indicators.note: in a down light, up means written bottom to top

parts.note: flew means hurried
to rest is to stay in bed
what's eating you means what's worrying you

explanation.surface: A patient hurried along but stayed in bed fretting over the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLEW into WELF. 'worried' is ATE, as in 'what's eating you?'. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's tax-funded health service is a central example of state provision of social security and care.

clue.text: Groundbreaker I used in wharf

indicators.note: the number is put to use inside the landing stage

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage, a wharf
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be a groundbreaker for using the waterfront.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer opens up new territory or methods, literally or figuratively breaking new ground.

clue.text: TV station securing opera about to broadcast

indicators.note: the station holds the reversed opera inside it

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

indicators.note: about signals turning the opera round

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A TV station secures rights to an opera it is about to air.
explanation.walkthrough: RTE is the Irish state broadcaster; 'about' looks like 'on the point of' but turns the opera round, which 'securing' then holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out in all directions, as signals or light spread from a source, is to spread widely.

clue.text: Last piece of music recorded twice by a UN secretary-general?

definitions.meaning: a closing section of a song or programme

definitions.text: recorded twice by a UN secretary-general
definitions.meaning: Boutros Boutros-Ghali had his first name written twice, and each Boutros holds these letters inside

explanation.surface: A UN chief's farewell tune is put on record twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: the letters sit inside Boutros, the name that Boutros Boutros-Ghali, sixth UN Secretary-General, has twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda that brings a track or broadcast to a close is the counterpart of an intro.

clue.text: Assessed situation of a Hobbit clan

definitions.meaning: paused to review how things stand
in Tolkien the Tooks are a Hobbit family

explanation.surface: Someone sized up the state of a Hobbit family.
explanation.definitionFit: To review one's circumstances is the idiom taken from counting a shop's inventory.

clue.text: Dispose of foolish nonsense in contrasting volumes

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the two volume markings

parts.note: in music p is piano (soft) and f is forte (loud)

indicators.note: the letters of the word are made into nonsense, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses silly talk delivered by turns softly and loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense' is the anagram signal for the word before it; the 'contrasting volumes' are the soft and loud markings in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off food or an opponent quickly and completely is idiomatically to see them off.

clue.text: Sentimental actor in summertime is captivated by rambling rose

indicators.note: held inside the shuffled flower
the flower's letters wander into a new order
the little word is put inside the time abbreviation

parts.note: BST is British Summer Time

explanation.surface: A sentimental actor in summer is charmed by a rambling rose.
explanation.walkthrough: BST, British Summer Time, is the clock in UK summers; 'rambling' suggests a climbing rose but scrambles it, and 'captivated by' places the time piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a journalist or performer given to tearjerking pathos, an emotional performer.

clue.text: Unmarked fruit kept in college is pulled out

indicators.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency, so taking away the mark drops it

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
at Oxford and Cambridge a student confined to college as punishment is gated

explanation.surface: Untouched fruit was kept in college and then pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxbridge gating confines an undergraduate to college, so 'kept in college' gives GATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched or drawn out lengthwise has been made longer.

clue.text: Bay where it all comes out?

definitions.meaning: a large square inlet of the North Sea on England's east coast
the truth will come out in the laundry, as the saying has it

explanation.surface: A bay where everything finally surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wash is the bay between Lincolnshire and Norfolk; 'it'll all come out in the laundry' is the idiom.

clue.text: Regularly tempt to cut garment lower

indicators.note: the picked letters cut into the garment

parts.note: a dress is a garment

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of tempt

explanation.surface: Tempted to shorten a dress by lowering its hem.
explanation.definitionFit: To press something down or reduce its level is to make it drop.

clue.text: Messenger's spoken, having lesson in two parts

indicators.note: spoken signals that the sound, not the spelling, is what counts

parts.note: a bearer carries a message; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A messenger speaks, giving a lesson in two parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'lesson' as 'less on': having less clothing on is being more naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing fewer clothes, with 'lesson' read as 'less on', leaves a person more uncovered.

clue.text: Over time, sailor gets trim

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman
to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: After a long time at sea, a sailor gets a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a position signal but is the definition, as in 'time over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Left over, in excess of what is needed, means extra or surplus.

clue.text: A kiss lifts me in Paris, as a rule

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: in a down light, lifting writes the word upwards

parts.note: moi is French for me

explanation.surface: A kiss in Paris lifts the spirits, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' turns MOI to IOM in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident principle accepted without proof serves as a basic law or maxim.

clue.text: Power couple return to America as sex symbol

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

indicators.note: return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pair is a couple
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A power couple goes back to America as celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapus is the Greek fertility god, always shown with an enormous phallus, a symbol of male virility.

clue.text: Letters from secretary, a Chinese native

definitions.meaning: a secretary is a PA, personal assistant, so its letters are P plus A, written out as a phrase
the black-and-white bear of the Sichuan bamboo forests

explanation.surface: A Chinese secretary sends letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the two letters of PA, a personal assistant, joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant bear of the bamboo forests of Sichuan is native to China, and is that country's emblem.

clue.text: Think tooth — it chewed

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
ate means chewed

explanation.surface: A broken tooth, and someone chews things over.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or meditate deeply is to reflect at length.

clue.text: Fail badly with a Japanese verse

parts.note: to tank is to fail badly

explanation.surface: A poet flops with a Japanese poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanka is a thirty-one-syllable Japanese poem, older cousin of the haiku.

clue.text: Act superficially, ordering makeshift cures

indicators.note: ordering puts letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A quack orders makeshift cures, acting superficially.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing only with the shallow aspects of something, never going deep, is acting superficially.
